sentences.text: In 2024, the influence index stands at 30.3 for China (band 23.8–56.7, from 4 of six components) and 23.7 for the United States (band 19.8–61.7, from 4 of six components). The net lean is +6.6 points toward China.
Over the five years to 2024, the index for China rose by 5.2 points and the index for the United States rose by 2.8 points.

The value for China rests on trade export share, trade import share, debt stock and diplomatic alignment; every component is a recorded tie (trade shares, finance, debt, UN votes, legislative stance), not a judgement.

The value for the United States rests on trade export share, trade import share, finance flow and diplomatic alignment; every component is a recorded tie (trade shares, finance, debt, UN votes, legislative stance), not a judgement.
In 2025, 96% of Guatemala's mineral exports (UN Comtrade value US$29 m) went to China and 0.0% to the United States; together 96%, the rest to other destinations.
Since 2020 the share going to China rose by 47.8 points and the share going to the United States was broadly flat.
Relative to the 20-country export basket, its exports are specialised in nickel (RCA 99.7) and rare earths (RCA 9.3).

8 sudden shifts in export shares are flagged from the customs data, the latest in 2019: Exports to the United States fell from 25% to 1% of the country's mineral exports between 2018 and 2019 (reported by GTM to UN Comtrade).

Since 2019, agreement with China was broadly flat and agreement with the United States rose by 6.7 points.
Too few mineral-related legislative records naming either actor have been scored for a stance series (five per year are needed); the text model is zero-shot baseline, not yet validated.

After Section 301 tariffs on imports from China, first tranche in force (2018-07), the share of exports to the United States moved -51.2 points (52% before, 1.2% after); placebo p 0.20 against the series' other years (event list still in draft). An association, not a cause.

After China: exports of gallium, germanium, antimony and superhard materials to the United States prohibited (Announcement 2024 No. 46) (2024-12), the share of exports to China moved +45.1 points (51% before, 96% after); placebo p 0.04 against the series' other years (event list still in draft). An association, not a cause.

After China: export controls on antimony items in force (Announcement 2024 No. 33 of 15 August 2024) (2024-09), the share of exports to China moved +45.1 points (51% before, 96% after); placebo p 0.04 against the series' other years (event list still in draft). An association, not a cause.

The published forecast for the share of mineral exports going to China in 2030 is 100% (90% band 58%–100%), from random walk with drift partially pooled across countries (empirical Bayes), which beat naive persistence by 13% CRPS in backtests; the last observed year is 2025.

The published forecast for the share of mineral exports going to the United States in 2030 is 0.0% (90% band 0.0%–58%), from naive persistence, because no model beat it in backtests; the last observed year is 2025.

The published forecast for the influence index of China in 2030 is 32.8 (90% band 23.8–44.5), from random walk with drift partially pooled across countries (empirical Bayes), which beat naive persistence by 1% CRPS in backtests; the last observed year is 2024.

The published forecast for the influence index of the United States in 2030 is 23.2 (90% band 0.0–49.5), from damped local linear trend (Kalman filter, maximum likelihood), which beat naive persistence by 2% CRPS in backtests; the last observed year is 2024.
Under the stated scenarios the 2030 median share to China ranges from 90% (US sourcing rules bite) to 100% (accelerated China pull); these are what-ifs with a fixed yearly shift, not predictions.

In 2025, unavailable components: legislative stance (no scored legislative records naming the actor); debt stock (no source for debt owed to the United States); finance flow (source coverage ends 2021); debt stock and diplomatic alignment (source coverage ends 2024).

Source coverage ends at different years: Chinese official finance to 2021, US finance to 2026, debt by creditor to 2024, UN votes to 2024 and trade to 2025; components beyond a source's coverage are unavailable, not zero.
